_comment: Seed league ids for the cross-league Manager Score corpus crawl. Sleeper has NO endpoint that enumerates leagues, and league ids are 19-digit snowflakes, so the id space cannot be swept. The only discovery path is the social graph: league -> /league/{id}/users -> /user/{user_id}/leagues/nfl/{season} -> their leagues -> their users. These are the entry points into that graph. See docs/CROSS-LEAGUE-CORPUS.md.
_why_not_leagues_json: leagues.json at the repo root is a PUBLISHING manifest, not a crawl frontier. Every entry there produces dynasty_site/leagues/<platform>-<id>.json and appears in the league.html selector, and it exists mainly because MFL has no CORS and must be baked in. The two files have different scope (MFL+Sleeper vs Sleeper-only), different lifecycle (hand-curated and small vs machine-extensible and growing), and different consumers (the league selector vs the corpus crawler). Adding crawl seeds to leagues.json would publish a per-league page for every seed and pollute the league picker with leagues nobody on this site asked to see. Kept separate on purpose.
_privacy: Only Sleeper display_name (a pseudonymous handle) is ever surfaced. No attempt is made to resolve a real identity. Data is read from Sleeper's public, read-only, unauthenticated API.

_durable_floor: This registry is the durable FLOOR on coverage. Crawl state (crawl_state.json) can be lost, reset or rolled over at a new season; every league ever confirmed dynasty is also recorded here, where only an explicit edit removes it. A cold start therefore re-reaches every known league for one call each instead of re-walking the social graph to rediscover them. Operators may add ids by hand; the crawl appends with --update-seeds; accepted issue submissions are appended by scripts/ingest_league_submissions.py.
_submission: Users submit a league id through a GitHub issue form (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/league-submission.yml). The ingest script validates the id against Sleeper before it is ever written here: it must be an existing NFL league with settings.type == 2. Issue text is parsed for digits only and is never executed, interpolated into a shell, or trusted for a league's name.
